column1: # *** THE NAVAL AND MERCHANT SERIES, SWEPT FOR NORTHAM AND BIDEFORD - 17 September 2026. ***
# Northam parish contains Appledore, so if the Taylor men went to sea they should be here.
# ADM 188 is indexed man by man and gives an EXACT DATE OF BIRTH, which makes it testable
# against a tree rather than merely suggestive.
# *** THE CONTROL IS THAT THE METHOD WORKS: it returned five named men of these two parishes
# with their dates of birth. *** So the null at the bottom is a tested null, not an untried one.

column3: *** ADM 188/195/140021 ***, Royal Navy register of seamen's services - *** THE DOCUMENT ITSELF, read 17 September 2026. *** O.N. 140021, Devonport. Born 14 Oct 1871, Northam. Engaged *** 14 October 1889 for 12 years ***, his eighteenth birthday. *** 5 ft 1 in, brown hair, brown eyes, fresh complexion, burn mark on back. *** Entered as a Boy on *** Lion, 29 January 1887 ***, aged 15. Then Shannon, Royal Adelaide, Vivid, *** Impregnable 20 May 1890 to 4 October 1892 ***, Melita, Sappho, Swift I, Royal Oak, Cambridge, Defiance, Curacoa. Promoted *** Acting Gunner ***; pension traced 18 January 1909.
column4: *** EXCLUDED, AND NOW BY THE DOCUMENT RATHER THAN BY AN INFERENCE. *** The catalogue rejection rested on a census age; the record gives two harder reasons. *** FIRST, the form asks for 'Names in full' and the answer is 'William Taylor' *** - our man is *** William JOHN Taylor ***, and the Navy had no reason to drop a middle name it had asked for. *** SECOND, AND IT IS CONCLUSIVE: on census night, 5 April 1891, this man was borne on HMS Impregnable at Devonport *** - he joined her 20 May 1890 and left 4 October 1892 - *** while William John Taylor was enumerated at home in Northam, aged 20. *** *** One man cannot be in two places on one night. They are two men. *** The near miss is closed.
No Joshua in this family. *** Not ours. ***
No Robert in this family. *** Not ours. ***
Born long after this generation. *** Not ours. ***

*** The only Brayley of Northam in the whole series. *** Born in the Gladstone years and named for him, as thousands were. Too late to be a sibling of Mary Ann Hellen Brayley (1843-1900) and *** unattached to her by any document ***, so he is recorded and not claimed.

column1: *** The Taylors of Appledore, in the merchant service ***
column3: Crew list of the *** Ulelia ***, official number 74429, National Maritime Museum: T Taylor, Mate, b.1846 Appledore; J W Taylor, Master, b.1888 Appledore; T G Taylor, Ordinary Seaman and Cook, b.1893 Appledore; previous ship *** Annie of Bideford. ***
column4: *** A SEAFARING TAYLOR FAMILY IN THE SAME PARISH, AND NOT ONE DOCUMENT JOINS THEM TO OURS. *** Appledore is in Northam. The generations are wrong for our men - ours are 1870 and 1872 - and *** no relationship is asserted. *** Recorded as context, and as a warning: a Taylor at sea out of Northam is not by itself our Taylor.

column1: *** WILLIAM JOHN TAYLOR (b. Nov 1870) and HORACE ARCHIBALD TAYLOR (b. Apr 1872) ***
column4: *** A TESTED NULL, AND A USEFUL ONE. *** Both parishes were swept, both spellings of the birthplace, and the series returned five other men by name and date while returning neither of these two. *** They were not Royal Navy ratings. *** If they went to sea it was the merchant service - and merchant crew lists are indexed by SHIP, not by man, which is a far harder search and should be costed before it is started.

column1: *** HOW THIS WAS READ, AND THE WALL THAT CAME DOWN HALFWAY ***
column3: Discovery's JSON API, then Discovery's own web search.
column4: *** The API answered 200 for about twenty queries and then began returning 202 with an empty body and the header `x-amzn-waf-action: challenge`. *** That is AWS bot detection, and it was not worked around: *** the control query itself started failing, so every zero collected at that moment was thrown away rather than recorded. *** The rest was done in a browser at reading pace, which is the access the catalogue is built for. *** Anyone scripting this again should expect the challenge after roughly twenty rapid calls and slow down well before it. ***

column1: *** WHAT COSTS MONEY AND WHAT DOES NOT ***
column4: The catalogue entry - name, exact date of birth, birthplace, year of entry - is *** free, and it is the part that does the genealogical work. *** The scanned service record is *** £3.50, or free to a signed-in TNA account ***, and shows ships, conduct and physical description. *** A watermarked preview is offered in their viewer and the image cannot be fetched outside it. *** No account was created and nothing was bought; that is David's call.
